events.title: The death of Raphael
events.shortBlurb: Raffaello Sanzio of Urbino, painter of the School of Athens and the Sistine Madonna, died on Good Friday at thirty-seven…
body: On Good Friday, 6 April 1520, Raphael died in Rome after a brief fever, aged thirty-seven — born, tradition holds, on the same day in 1483 at Urbino. His body lay in state in his studio beside his last, unfinished canvas, the Transfiguration, and all Rome mourned the 'divine painter.'

Summoned to Rome by Julius II about 1508, he had frescoed the Stanze of the Vatican — the School of Athens and the Disputà among them — painted the Sistine Madonna and the Galatea, and on Bramante's death in 1514 been made chief architect of the new St. Peter's then rising.

He was buried, as he had asked, in the Pantheon, the ancient temple become the church of Santa Maria ad Martyres, where his tomb still bears Cardinal Bembo's epitaph: here lies Raphael; while he lived, great Nature feared to be outdone, and when he died, she feared to die herself.
